source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM agents are experiential learners
finding: Ablation of how past trajectories are chosen in ALFWorld: task-similarity retrieval beats reasoning-step similarity and random sampling.
numbers: ALFWorld success rate, gpt-3.5 agent: ReAct no memory 40.0; random successful trajectories 42.5; reason-similarity retrieval 48.5; task-similarity retrieval (ExpeL) 59.0. Mean over 4 folds.
limits: One benchmark, one small model (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613). Random sampling still gave +2.5 over no memory. Row order in the extracted table was inferred from the text.
agent_relevance: Case retrieval by task similarity is worth about 16 points over random in this setting. Index the subgoal library by task, not by the last thought.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM agents are experiential learners
finding: Abstracted insights and retrieved raw cases are complementary; which one matters depends on the task.
numbers: Insights-only vs retrieval-only success: HotpotQA 36% vs 31%; ALFWorld 50% vs 55%; WebShop 37% vs 38%. Full ExpeL HotpotQA 39.0 vs ReAct 28.0.
limits: Small gaps, standard errors around 1-2 points. Insight extraction needed a stronger model (gpt-4); gpt-3.5 insights were worse; adding reflections to extraction hurt.
agent_relevance: Keep both a case (concrete trajectory) and a rule (abstracted note) in the library; do not drop either.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM agents are experiential learners
finding: Insight extraction needs real experience: extracting only from the original few-shot examples gave no gain over ReAct.
numbers: Agent extracting insights only from initial few-shot examples showed no advantage over ReAct on HotpotQA; agents with gathered success/failure pairs did significantly better (Fig. 6).
limits: Figure values not read exactly. HotpotQA only.
agent_relevance: Library value comes from the agent's own run history with success/failure pairs, not from seeded examples.

source: Fang et al. (2026) Memp: Exploring agent procedural memory
finding: Random retrieval of stored procedures is worse than similarity retrieval and can be worse than no memory on hard constraints.
numbers: TravelPlanner, GPT-4o: no memory commonsense 71.93 / hard-constraint 12.88; random sample 74.59 / 6.72; key=query 73.38 / 8.95; key=AveFact (keyword-averaged) 76.02 / 8.25. Qwen2.5-72b hard-constraint: none 7.34, random 8.43, query 11.97, AveFact 12.66.
limits: Hard-constraint scores fell below the no-memory baseline for GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-sonnet under every memory policy, so memory raised one metric and lowered another there.
agent_relevance: Track the hard checks separately from soft scores (G3, G7).

source: Fang et al. (2026) Memp: Exploring agent procedural memory
finding: Storing a distilled procedure beats storing a script alone or the raw trajectory alone, mainly on ALFWorld.
numbers: ALFWorld test success, GPT-4o: no memory 42.14; script 56.43; trajectory 74.29; proceduralization (both) 77.86; steps 23.76 -> 15.01. Claude-3.5-sonnet 34.97 -> 74.72. Qwen2.5-72b 41.25 -> 77.19.
limits: ALFWorld tasks come in templates, so near-duplicate tasks favour reuse. TravelPlanner gains were small (commonsense +8 at best).
agent_relevance: Template-heavy task streams reward a case library strongly. Expect smaller gains on one-off problems.

source: Fang et al. (2026) Memp: Exploring agent procedural memory
finding: More retrieved procedures help, then plateau, and too many hurt.
numbers: GPT-4o ALFWorld: success rises with number retrieved (0 to 20) up to a plateau, then declines; authors blame context length and less accurate memories.
limits: Exact peak not read from figure.
agent_relevance: Cap retrieved cases at a small k (see Memento k=4).

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: fine-tuning LLM agents without fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Case-bank retrieval gives additive gains over planning alone on three benchmarks; the best number of cases is small.
numbers: Memento vs same system without CBR (F1/PM): HLE 26.7/24.4 vs 22.2/17.4; SimpleQA 84.7/95.0 vs 81.0/89.7; DeepResearcher 66.6/80.4 vs 59.9/72.2. K cases on DeepResearcher: K=0 59.9/72.2; K=1 63.6/77.9; K=4 64.5/78.5 (best); K=32 63.9/78.1.
limits: Authors flag data contamination on DeepResearcher. Most of the gain comes from the first case. K was tuned on the same benchmark it is reported on.
agent_relevance: Retrieve 1 to 4 cases. More adds noise, unlike few-shot prompting.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: fine-tuning LLM agents without fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Learned (Q-function) case selection beats plain similarity retrieval slightly; both beat no CBR over five learning rounds.
numbers: DeepResearcher over 5 iterations: no CBR 78.65 -> 84.47; similarity CBR 79.84 -> 84.85; learned-Q CBR 80.46 -> 85.44. Gap to no-CBR shrinks from 1.2-1.8 points to 0.4-1.0.
limits: Gaps are small and shrink with iterations; no variance reported. The no-CBR arm also gains 5.8 points over rounds, so not all learning is from cases.
agent_relevance: Learned per-case utility is a modest gain over similarity. Most of the gain is plain similarity.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: fine-tuning LLM agents without fine-tuning LLMs
finding: On GAIA the case bank was filled on the validation set, then the test result is reported from that bank.
numbers: GAIA validation 87.88% Pass@3 (three iterations storing successes and failures); test 79.40% using only the bank built on validation.
limits: Pass@3 over iterations is not a single-shot number. Closed planner and executor (GPT-4.1, o3). No no-CBR arm on GAIA in the text read.
agent_relevance: Report single-shot results with a frozen bank when judging our library.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How memory management impacts LLM agents: experience-following
finding: Agents copy retrieved experience: output similarity tracks input similarity almost perfectly when memory is dense.
numbers: Pearson r close to 1 between input similarity and output similarity for retrieved records (RegAgent, AgentDriver, EHRAgent, CIC-IoT); fixed-memory baseline shows low similarity on both.
limits: Some agents are synthetic. Main backbone GPT-4o-mini; GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 show the same pattern in the appendix.
agent_relevance: Retrieval is not neutral advice. The model copies the nearest case, mistakes included.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How memory management impacts LLM agents: experience-following
finding: Errors in stored cases propagate: add-all, or a coarse LLM judge as filter, leaves a growing gap to an error-free memory.
numbers: Gap versus error-free (ground-truth output) memory appears immediately and widens under add-all and coarse selective addition. Strict-evaluator addition on AgentDriver closes the gap over time.
limits: Exact gaps are in figures, not read. A coarse LLM evaluator was worse than a small hand-built high-quality set.
agent_relevance: Write a case only after a code check passes, never on model self-judgment (G2, G5).

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How memory management impacts LLM agents: experience-following
finding: Deleting cases by usage history plus utility can beat keeping everything, and with a strict evaluator can beat the error-free memory.
numbers: Table 2 (garbled layout) strict-evaluator rows: no deletion about 70.95 with memory 2938 vs combined deletion about 69.8 with much smaller memory; CIC-IoT 85.4 no deletion vs 89.6 for one deletion method.
limits: Pdftotext scrambled Table 2 so column mapping is not certain. Under a coarse or noisy evaluator, history-based deletion degraded results.
agent_relevance: Prune low-utility cases; the value depends on how reliable the success signal is.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026) ReasoningBank
finding: Storing distilled strategies from successes and failures beats raw-trajectory memory (Synapse) and successful workflows (AWM) on WebArena; the baselines gain little.
numbers: WebArena overall SR, Gemini-2.5-flash: none 40.5; Synapse 42.1; AWM 44.1; ReasoningBank 48.8; +MaTTS 51.8. Gemini-2.5-pro: 46.7 / 47.7 / 47.6 / 53.9 / 56.3. Claude-3.7-sonnet: 41.7 / 42.6 / 40.8 / 46.3 / 48.8.
limits: Same group proposes ReasoningBank, so baselines may be under-tuned. 684 tasks, single run per cell, no confidence intervals.
agent_relevance: Independent re-run of AWM and Synapse shows smaller gains than AWM's own paper. Treat published case-memory gains as upper bounds.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026) ReasoningBank
finding: Failures help only when the memory format can use them: raw-trajectory memories gain little or lose when failures are added.
numbers: WebArena-Shopping, Gemini-2.5-flash: Synapse 40.6 (success only) -> 41.7 (with failures); AWM degraded; ReasoningBank 46.5 -> 49.7.
limits: One subset (187 tasks).
agent_relevance: Store failures as a short note on what went wrong, not as a case to imitate.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026) ReasoningBank
finding: Result is robust to a noisy success judge in the 70-90% accuracy range.
numbers: LLM judge accuracy against ground truth was 72.7%; simulated judge accuracies 100 down to 50% gave success rates between about 47 and 49.7; ground-truth labels gave the best.
limits: Simulation only; one subset.
agent_relevance: A 70%-accurate success label may be enough for strategy notes, but not for raw cases (see Xiong et al.).

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Induced abstract workflows beat a no-memory baseline and a method that retrieves concrete similar examples.
numbers: WebArena, GPT-4: AWM 35.5% vs BrowserGym baseline 23.5% (+12.0 points, +51.1% relative); SteP with human workflows 32.0%. Mind2Web cross-task step SR: MindAct 36.2 -> AWM 45.1 (gpt-4); Synapse (retrieves concrete examples) 30.6 -> AWM 34.6 (gpt-3.5), +4.0.
limits: The independent ReasoningBank run found AWM +3.6 (Gemini flash), +0.9 (Gemini pro), -0.9 (Claude). Mind2Web full-task success is very low (0.7 to 4.8%).
agent_relevance: Abstract sub-routines may bias the agent less than concrete cases. Cheap to test against our case library.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Online workflows (from the model's own unlabelled runs) match or beat offline workflows as the train-test gap widens, but wrong workflows can hurt.
numbers: Mind2Web cross-domain step SR: MindAct 18.6; AWM offline 32.6; AWM online 35.5. Cross-website 30.1 / 33.7 / 33.9. In-domain cross-task offline is slightly better (45.1 vs 43.6).
limits: Online induction depends on an automatic success judge; the authors say its errors can produce incorrect workflows that degrade performance.
agent_relevance: A bad success label makes a bad case, so retain only after a check.

source: Liu et al. (2022) What makes good in-context examples for GPT-3? (KATE)
finding: Nearest-neighbour example choice beats random in-context examples; retrievers tuned on a related task beat generic ones.
numbers: IMDB sentiment accuracy, GPT-3: random 87.95 +- 2.74; KATE RoBERTa 91.99; KATE NLI 90.40; KATE tuned on SST-2 93.43. Abstract: relative gains 41.9% on ToTTo and 45.5% on Natural Questions over random.
limits: Early GPT-3 (2021), 2-3 examples, temperature 0. Pure kNN label voting without the model scored 50.20 on IMDB and was far worse than random on generation tasks, so the model still does the work.
agent_relevance: Similarity retrieval is a strong default for example choice; copying the nearest case's label alone is not enough.

source: Liu et al. (2022) What makes good in-context examples for GPT-3? (KATE)
finding: Which examples are shown moves results a lot: random sets gave wide run-to-run variance, and the nearest examples beat the farthest.
numbers: Random-set accuracy varied widely across draws (see the +-2.74 above); closest 10 vs farthest 10 training examples (100 test questions) showed nearest better.
limits: Exact nearest/farthest numbers not extracted; small test subset.
agent_relevance: Fix the retrieval rule in code; the choice of cases is itself a source of variance.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large language models as analogical reasoners
finding: Asking the model to recall its own relevant problems (self-generated cases) before solving beats 0-shot and fixed few-shot CoT, and is claimed to beat retrieved-exemplar CoT, especially for larger models.
numbers: Average gain about +4% over baselines on GSM8K, MATH, Codeforces and BIG-Bench with GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4 and PaLM2. Codeforces for GPT-4 was about equal to 3-shot CoT (Acc@1 16% vs 16%).
limits: Table cells scrambled by text extraction. Codeforces gains are within a point for GPT-4. Gains depend on model strength.
agent_relevance: Self-generated cases are cheap but unverified. Good as a cold start before the library has entries; add a code check.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) Self-generated in-context examples improve LLM agents
finding: Naive accumulation of the agent's own successful trajectories, retrieved by similarity, lifts success on three benchmarks; the gain is about a model upgrade.
numbers: ALFWorld 73% -> 89%, Wordcraft 55% -> 64%, InterCode-SQL 75% -> 79% (gpt-4o-mini; mean of 5 seeds). With database and exemplar curation, ALFWorld 93%, above AutoManual 79%.
limits: Diminishing returns: most gain in the first 25% of added tasks. Some added trajectories lowered performance; cross-trial variance was large. ALFWorld has repeated task types.
agent_relevance: Library growth saturates fast; utility-based curation is needed.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) Self-generated in-context examples improve LLM agents
finding: Curating by a retrieval-weighted outcome score per stored trajectory improves on blind accumulation.
numbers: ALFWorld: Fixed-DB 0.72; Traj-Bootstrap about 0.91 at 3500 tasks; with exemplar curation up to 0.93. Table row mapping partly scrambled in extraction.
limits: Score = outcomes of tasks where the case was retrieved, weighted by retrieval frequency; needs many tasks to estimate.
agent_relevance: This is a measured retain/revise rule; use it to decide what stays in the subgoal library.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet
finding: Plain similarity retrieval of past question-answer pairs (DR) helps one model and hurts another; curated memory is more reliable.
numbers: Claude 3.5 Sonnet GPQA-Diamond: BL 59.6, DR 63.6, DC-RS 68.7. GPT-4o: Game of 24 BL 10.0, DR 6.0, DC-RS 99.0; GPQA BL 57.1, DR 55.1; MMLU-Pro Eng BL 53.2, DR 48.8; AIME 2024 BL 20.0, DR 26.7.
limits: Tiny sets (AIME 30 questions), single run. Authors say retrieval can confuse when suboptimal examples are recalled. DC-RS gains on Game of 24 come from a reusable code routine, not case similarity.
agent_relevance: Raw similarity retrieval can lower accuracy. Store reusable procedures, not only solved instances.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet
finding: Appending the full history (no curation) hurts.
numbers: AIME 2024: Claude BL 23.3, FH 26.7, DC 50.0; GPT-4o BL 20.0, FH 6.7, DC-RS 40.0.
limits: Single run, 30 questions; one question = 3.3 points.
agent_relevance: Do not dump all past cases into the prompt.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager
finding: A skill library retrieved by embedding similarity is needed for long-run progress; the retrieval itself is accurate.
numbers: Skill retrieval over 309 samples: top-1 accuracy 80.2 +- 3.0, top-5 96.5 +- 0.3. Without the skill library exploration plateaus late; a random curriculum cuts items found by 93%.
limits: Minecraft only; ablation shown as curves, three runs. Library entries are verified executable code.
agent_relevance: Verified, executable entries make retrieval safe.

source: Wiratunga et al. (2024) CBR-RAG
finding: Hybrid case retrieval raised answer similarity only slightly over no retrieval.
numbers: Open Australian legal QA, 32 test cases, Mistral-7B: cosine to reference no-RAG 0.8967; best hybrid AnglEBERT k=3 full case 0.9141 (+1.94%); significant vs no-RAG at 95% (one-tailed t-test), at 90% vs hybrid BERT k=1.
limits: Only 32 test cases; scored by embedding similarity, not factual accuracy; k was tuned on the same cases; strong parametric memory makes the baseline high.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence. Judge case retrieval by outcomes, not text similarity.

source: Yin and Leake (2026) Capturing LLM cases for RAG reuse
finding: Case capture with only right/wrong feedback improved some models on MMLU subsets; a second feedback round did not help consistently.
numbers: Six LLMs on MMLU history (687), science (750), math (548). Examples: Llama-3.1-8B history 76.9 -> 82.1, math 58.0 -> 60.9 (single) -> 63.9 (double); gpt-4.1-nano history 82.1 -> 85.0. Four trials significant vs baseline in single mode; three trials where double beat single; six trials where double was lower (not significant). McNemar test.
limits: Curves track baseline for the first questions then diverge. Gains vary by model and subject; gpt-3.5 math appears lower with cases (66.9 -> 64.3). Workshop paper; one retrieved case per question.
agent_relevance: One round of real feedback is worth it. Do not add rounds by default (fits G1).

source: Hu et al. (2024) Case-based or rule-based: how do transformers do the math?
finding: Transformers solve arithmetic by matching seen cases, not rules: leaving out a block of training cases collapses accuracy even though over 95% of the data remains.
numbers: Leave-Square-Out test on addition and other tasks: accuracy drops sharply inside the removed block while random split stays near 100%. Rule-Following Fine-Tuning: training on 1-5 digit addition generalises to 12-digit above 95%, over 40 points above scratchpad.
limits: Implicit case-matching in weights, mostly GPT-2 on small tasks. Not the same as an external case base.
agent_relevance: Models lean on near-neighbour cases. Putting the rule in the prompt beats showing examples of the rule.

source: Review of case-based reasoning for LLM agents (2025)
finding: Survey claims CBR-augmented agents do better on specialised tasks but gives no new measurements and says benchmarks are missing.
numbers: Cites DS-Agent 100% development-stage success and 99% one-pass rate with GPT-4; says evaluation frameworks for CBR agents remain an open challenge.
limits: Secondary claims; no controls or variance. Treat listed gains as unverified.
agent_relevance: Use primary results above, not survey-level claims.

source: Aamodt and Plaza (1994) Case-based reasoning: foundational issues
finding: Defines the retrieve, reuse, revise, retain cycle that the LLM papers above implement.
numbers: No numbers; framework paper. A fetch of a PDF copy returned HTTP 404, so not opened.
limits: Not opened this session.
agent_relevance: Our S9 record maps to retain; revise maps to checked repair.

source: Gick and Holyoak (1980) Analogical problem solving
finding: Classic human result: people rarely use a similar solved case unless told it is relevant.
numbers: Not opened. Exact percentages not verified, so none recorded.
limits: Numbers unverified; do not cite without opening.
agent_relevance: Supports a program-driven retrieval step instead of waiting for the model to notice a relevant case.

source: Ross (1984) Remindings and their effects in learning a cognitive skill
finding: Learners were reminded of earlier examples by surface features, which shaped later problem solving.
numbers: Not opened; no numbers recorded.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Surface similarity can fetch the wrong case; index by structure as well.
